claims.claim: Athanasius was born c. 296–298 in Alexandria, Roman Egypt, and died on 2 May 373 in Alexandria.
Athanasius was also called Athanasius the Great, Athanasius the Confessor, or, among Coptic Christians, Athanasius the Apostolic.
The Letter to Maximus was written about 371 A.D.
The letter was addressed to Maximus, a philosopher, whom Athanasius calls 'our beloved and most truly longed-for son.'
Athanasius wrote the letter in response to Maximus's own letter, yielding reluctantly to Maximus's zeal for the truth in view of the argumentativeness of shameless men.
Athanasius states that he dictated nothing beyond what Maximus's letter contains, in order that the adversary may be convinced on the points to which he has objected.
The letter urges adherence to what was confessed at Nicaea by the Fathers.
Athanasius was known as the greatest champion of Catholic belief on the subject of the Incarnation and earned the title 'Father of Orthodoxy' for his defense against Arianism.
